segments.text: Listening Test In the listening test, you will be asked
to demonstrate how well you understand spoken English.
The entire listening test will last approximately 45 minutes.
There are four parts and directions are given for each part.
You must mark your answers on the separate answer sheet.
Do not write your answers in your test book.
Part 1.
Directions For each question in this part, you will
hear four statements about a picture in your test book.
When you hear the statements, you must select the one statement that best describes what
you see in the picture.
Then find the number of the question on your answer sheet and mark your answer.
The statements will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Now part 1 will begin.
Number 1.
Look at the picture marked number 1 in your test book.
Some armchairs are facing a window.
A curtain is being drawn across a window.
A seating area is illuminated by lamps.
Some magazines have been left on a table.
Number 2.
Look at the picture marked number 2 in your test book.
A. They're viewing some paintings.
B. They're reading some brochures.
C. They're hanging some signs.
D. They're sorting some papers.
Number 3. Look at the picture marked number 3 in your test book.
A. The woman is turning on a lamp.
B. The woman is answering a telephone.
C. Folders are stacked on a chair.
D. There is a bulletin board above a desk.
Number 4. Look at the picture marked number 4 in your test book.
A. They're stacking some folders on a table.
B. They're looking at a white board.
C. One of the men is typing on a laptop.
D. One of the men is lifting a mug.
Number 5. Look at the picture marked number 5 in your test book.
A. A ladder is lying on the ground.
B. A window is being cleaned.
C. Some bicycles are parked in a garage.
D. An awning is being installed.
Number 6. Look at the picture marked number 6 in your test book.
A. A cashier is scanning an item.
B. A cashier is counting songs.
C. A customer is pushing a cart.
D. A customer is filling a bag with groceries.
Part 2. Directions.
You will hear a question or statement and three responses spoken in English.
They will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time.
Select the best response to the question or statement and mark the letter A, B or C on your answer sheet.
Now, let us begin with question number 7.
Number 7.
Where can I pick up my conference badge?
A. It only takes a couple of minutes.
B. Yes, they're printing the badges now.
C. The greeter near the entrance can point you there.
Number 8.
Where did the owner decide to put the new outdoor seating area?
A.
Right after the staff meeting.
B. Because customers kept requesting it.
C. Out along the west side.
Number 9.
Are you moving into the new apartment this Saturday or waiting until the first of next month?
A. I found it through a co-worker.
B. The ceremony was really moving.
C. My lease doesn't start until the first.
Number 10.
Would you like just one copy of this poster or shall I make you two?
A. I'll just take a single thanks.
B. The poster turned out really well.
C. Yes, sometime this afternoon.
Number 11.
When does the next dolphin show usually begin?
A.
In about half an hour.
B. Just past the touch tank area.
C. No, they're kept near the shore.
Number 12.
The dinner trays will be delivered before the guests sit down, right?
A. The trains run every 20 minutes.
B. There are 40 guests on the list.
C. Yes, the vans arriving at 6.
Number 13.
Honestly, I didn't expect Franklin's answers to be that impressive.
A. She answered on the first ring.
B. Sure, let's schedule another round.
C. Yes, and his examples were very specific too.
Number 14.
The extended warranties included in this price, isn't it?
A.
The meeting concluded right on time.
B. No, that's actually an extra charge.
C. They picked up the top price.
Number 15.
What do we need to bring to the first painting class?
A. Isn't there a list on the sign-up page?
B. They're painting the hallway tomorrow.
C. Yes, she's a wonderful teacher.
Number 16.
Why don't we have lunch brought in so we can keep working?
A. Sure, that'd save us some time.
B. It was delicious, thanks.
C. At the restaurant across the street.
Number 17.
Did we decide to take the train or fly up to the regional office next week?
A. We really didn't want to risk any delays at the airport.
B. The regional office just finished a big renovation.
C. Let's train the new hires before that trip.
Number 18.
You haven't cleared the puzzle room between bookings yet, have you?
A. The puzzles are all pretty tricky.
B. Yes, it's clear outside now.
C. Was that on my list?
Number 19.
Should I close the blinds?
A. That one's stuck too.
B. I'll turn the lights off instead.
C. The blueprints look fine.
Number 20.
Why don't we share a taxi to the trade show instead of waiting for the shuttle?
A. Because it needs a new chair.
B. It's just past the main station.
C. That works for me.
Number 21.
Haven't the microscope been cleaned yet?
A. We took care of that yesterday afternoon.
B. Sure, I'd be glad to help.
C. They're pretty fragile, actually.
Number 22.
I've got a spare charger with me if your phone's running low.
A. This one's a bit larger, actually.
B. There's an outlet right behind you.
C. Thanks, but mine's still nearly full.
Number 23.
Why won't the doe mixer start up this morning?
A. The backup mixers are kept in the back room.
B. I ran into the same thing with mine last week.
C. Our morning shift starts at 6.
Number 24.
When do advanced tickets for the new film go on sale?
A. We sailed along the coast last month.
B. Not until this weekend, apparently.
C. Yes, right by the main entrance.
Number 25.
This afternoon's session is being recorded for later, isn't it?
A. It should finish around 5.
B. She set a new sales record last month.
C. The audio-visual team would know.
Number 26.
Do you have a mallet I could borrow?
A. I lent mine to Owen.
B. How long did that last?
C. A few spare pegs, thanks.
Number 27.
You still haven't heard back from the fabric supplier about that delayed order, have you?
A. No, they haven't gotten back to us.
B. The dinner was quite delightful.
C. A bolt of gray wool.
Number 28.
Why are there so few cars in the parking lot this morning?
A. Aren't most people at the training session today?
B. Sure, whenever you're ready.
C. He's driving the new van today.
Number 29.
The dryers over there haven't finished the cycle yet, have they?
A. It's $1.50 per load.
B. Yes, they just stopped a minute ago.
C. No, I came on my bicycle.
Number 30.
Have you thought about switching to the digital menu boards?
A. Wouldn't that confuse our regular customers?
B. Yes, I got a little board waiting.
C. The kitchen is right through there.
Number 31.
Shouldn't we lower the prices on these leftover shrubs?
A. Over by the back fence.
B. No, the manager has to approve that first.
C. The flowers look lovely today.
Part 3.
Directions. You will hear some conversations between two or more people.
You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation.
Select the best response to each question and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet.
The conversations will not be printed in your testbook and will be spoken only one time.
Questions 32 through 34 refer to the following conversation.
Good morning Northgate radio. How can I help you?
Hi, this is Hannah Prescott. I entered your morning trivia contest yesterday and someone called me last night to say I'd won.
Yes, congratulations. Your prize package includes two concert tickets, a $30 gift card, and one of our station t-shirts.
That's wonderful. How do I go about picking everything up?
I'd be happy to mail the package straight to your home.
Or if you prefer, you can drop by our front desk any weekday afternoon.
Number 32.
Where does the man most likely work?
Number 33.
What did the woman recently do?
Number 34.
What does the man propose to do?
Questions 35 through 37 refer to the following conversation.
Hi. I bought two tickets for the 7 o'clock showing tonight, but something's come up and we can't make it.
Is it possible to change them to a later time?
Of course. Let me pull that up.
Which film is it for and what time would you like instead?
It's for the new adventure movie. If there's anything around 9, that would be great as long as we can still sit together.
Let me check.
Yes, the 915 screening has two seats side by side. There's just a small difference though.
The evening shows cost $2 more per ticket, so that's $4 in total.
That's fine. What do I need to do?
Just hand me your old tickets and step to the side and I'll print the new ones for you in a moment.
Number 35.
Where does the conversation most likely take place?
Number 36.
What does the man want to do?
Number 37.
What will the man most likely do next?
Questions 38 through 40 refer to the following conversation.
Good afternoon. Welcome to Larkfield Portrait Studio. How can I help you today?
Hi. I'd like to book a family portrait session. Ideally sometime this weekend.
Sure. We have openings both Saturday and Sunday morning. How many people will be in the photo?
There'll be four of us. It's for my parents' anniversary, so we'd like something a bit special.
Wonderful. We offer two packages.
The standard one is a 30-minute session with digital photos only.
The premium one runs a full hour and includes a set of printed photos as well.
Let's go with the premium package. Oh, and how soon will the pictures be ready?
About a week for the prints. And one last thing. Please arrive 15 minutes early so we can go over the poses before we start.
Number 38.
Where most likely does the man work?
Number 39.
Why is the woman speaking with the man?
Number 40.
What does the man tell the woman to do before the session begins?
Questions 41 through 43 refer to the following conversation.
Good morning. I'm calling to confirm a group visit we booked at the Kent Mere Museum.
My name is Douglas Reeve and I'm bringing my class this Thursday the 14th.
I just wanted to make sure everything is still in order.
Let me check for you.
Yes, Mr. Reeve, I can see your booking right here for a group of 30 students on Thursday morning.
Your visit also includes a guided tour of the main exhibit hall and one of our staff members will meet your group at the entrance.
That's wonderful. Thank you.
One more thing. Is there a place where they could eat their packed lunches after the tour?
We'd like to stay a bit longer if there's space available.
Number 41.
Why is the man calling?
Number 42.
Who will be visiting the museum?
Number 43.
What does the man ask about at the end of the conversation?
Questions 44 through 46 refer to the following conversation.
Thanks for calling Ridgeline, Lon and Garden. This is Trevor. How can I help you today?
Hi. I'd like to book an autumn leaf cleanup for my property.
It's a cornalot with quite a few large maple trees in the back.
Sure, we can take care of that. I should mention though that we're very busy this season.
The next regular opening is about three weeks out.
Three weeks? That's longer than I was hoping. Is there anything sooner available?
We do have weekend slots that open up faster, but there's an extra $40 for those.
We also offer a three-visit autumn package. The per-visit rate is lower and we could start next week.
Let me think it over before I decide.
Could you email me the details for both options? I'll look through them tonight.
Number 44.
What service does the woman want to arrange?
Number 45.
Why is the woman postponing her decision?
Number 46.
What does the woman say she will do next?
Questions 47 through 49 refer to the following conversation.
Hi, Bradley. The customer survey results came in this morning.
We've got responses from the last three months.
One request came up over and over.
People want more places to sit and read while they're browsing.
More seating? Camille, I agree it would be nice, but where would we possibly fit extra chairs?
Every corner of the floor is already used for something.
You have a point. It is tight.
What if we moved the new releases table, though?
It's sitting right by the front window, and that whole area could easily hold a couple of armchairs.
Hmm, that could actually work.
We could shift the new releases table over near the main aisle, where customers walk in first.
It would probably draw even more attention there.
Good thinking.
Let me put together a quick floor plan sketch this afternoon and send it over to our store manager, Ms. Langley, for approval.
47. Where most likely do the speakers work?
48. What does the man mean when he says, where would we possibly fit extra chairs?
49. What does the woman offer to do?
Questions 50 through 52 refer to the following conversation.
Ms. Reyes, I finished drafting the agenda for next week's training workshop last night.
I left a copy on your desk if you'd like to look it over this morning.
Oh, that's great. Thanks for getting that done so quickly.
The one thing we still haven't sorted out is who's going to present which part.
The new hires are arriving on Monday, so we really need to lock that down.
What are you thinking?
Well, I'd suggest you take the opening section on our company policies,
since you've been running new hire orientations for years and you know that material inside out.
I can handle the software demonstration in the second half.
It shouldn't add much to your plate. I only need about an hour today to pull my slides together.
50. What did the man recently finish?
51. Where most likely are the speakers?
52. What does the man suggest doing?
Questions 53 through 55 refer to the following conversation with three speakers.
Hi there. My colleague and I are trying to use the projector in the conference room down the hall,
but it just won't connect to our laptop.
We've got a client presentation in about 20 minutes, so we're a little stuck.
Oh, that's a known issue with the older units on that floor.
The connection port tends to fail.
Rather than troubleshoot it now, why don't I lend you one of our spare loaner projectors?
It'll connect right away.
That would be a lifesaver. Thank you.
Simon, does that work for you?
Absolutely. In the meantime, we can go back and get our slides loaded up and ready to run.
Perfect. Go ahead and head to the room.
I'll bring the loaner over to conference room three and set it up for you in just a few minutes.
53. Where most likely are the speakers?
54. What does the woman offer to provide?
55. What will the men most likely do next?
Questions 56 through 58 refer to the following conversation with three speakers.
Hi, come on in. Sorry about all the noise out front.
We've got a crew taking down that old tree in the driveway this morning,
so please just watch your step.
Not a problem at all.
So we're here to walk through the kitchen remodel, correct?
I've put together some preliminary ideas based on the photos and measurements you sent over last week.
Wonderful. The two big things I really want are a lot more storage.
I'm completely out of cabinet space and a much bigger window above the sink.
The one there now is far too small.
Both of those are definitely doable.
The new window will take a little more planning because of the wall behind it.
So let me bring in my colleague on that side.
This is Ethan Beckett, our design consultant.
Nice to meet you.
I've actually already put together three different window layouts for you.
Let me pull them up on my tablet.
You'll be able to see how each one would look from inside the room.
56. What project are the speakers discussing?
Where do the men most likely work?
58. What will the woman most likely do next?
Questions 59-61 refer to the following conversation.
Excuse me. Could you tell me what time the penguin feeding starts today?
It's at 2.30.
I should mention though that this week the feeding is being held at the South Gallery, not at the main viewing hall like usual.
Oh, the South Gallery.
I already told my group to meet me at the main hall entrance.
That's right. The main viewing hall is closed for maintenance this week.
Crews are upgrading the overhead lighting system, so all the feeding shows are running from the South Gallery until Friday.
I see. While I'm here, could I also book a spot on the behind the scenes tour this afternoon?
Certainly. We still have room. Only two spots left actually.
Today's tour focuses on our sea turtle rehabilitation program, and it'll be led by Dr Fowler, one of our biologists who just returned from a field research trip along the coast.
59. Where does the conversation most likely take place?
60. Why does the man say the South Gallery?
61. According to the woman, why has the feeding show been moved?
Questions 62 through 64 refer to the following conversation with three speakers and priceless.
Hi. A friend recommended Red Brook Tile Studio. I'm redoing the floor in my bathroom, and I'd like to buy some tile. There are so many options here.
Which one would work best for a bathroom?
For a bathroom, you'll really want something slip resistant. The slate finish has a textured surface, so it won't get slippery when it's wet. That's the one I'd recommend.
Oh, that sounds perfect. I'll take enough boxes for the whole room then. And once I've bought it, can someone come and put it in for me?
Yes, we offer a full installation service. I can have one of our teams come out this Thursday morning if that works for you.
Thursday morning is great. Let's set that up. Thank you both so much.
62. What type of business is being described?

All right, I can help with that. We have this chart comparing our four cookware sets. It shows which ones are non-stick, which ones are dishwasher safe, and the price of each.
63. What's the most you'd like to spend?

63. Question 68 through 70 refer to the following conversation and list.
63. Hi. I'd like to rent a private office here for my team. Is that something you can help me with at the front desk?
63. Absolutely. I can help you with that right now. First, how many people are on your team?
63. There are six of us. We actually just expanded. We started with four people last year and business has been going really well.
63. Congratulations. Let me look at our list of private offices. We have one that comfortably fits a team of exactly six. You can see it here on the chart.
63. That sounds perfect. How soon could we move in?
63. The office is available at the start of next month. To reserve it though, we'll need a security deposit from you today.
63. No problem. I can take care of the deposit right now. Thanks.

71. Through 73. Refer to the following announcement.

77-79. Refer to the following broadcast.
It's time now for everyone's favorite part of the morning here on Sunrise Radio, our weekly listener giveaway.
This week, one lucky listener will win a pair of tickets to the Brookmere Summer Music Festival, along with a backstage tour on opening night.
To enter, all you have to do is call our studio line and tell us the name of your all-time favorite song. And honestly, it's as easy as that.
We'll draw the winning name live on the air this Friday, so be sure you're tuned in.
Coming up right after the break, we'll be chatting with local chef Adele Hoffman about her brand new cookbook.
Stay with us, and the best of luck to everyone.

Questions 98-100 refer to the following excerpt from a meeting and chart.
Good morning everyone.
Now that the results of our users survey are in, I'd like to walk you through them.
We ran the survey to learn which parts of our app people actually rely on, so we can decide where to focus our efforts.
Please take a look at the chart on the screen.

16% of users told us they still depend on a feature we have barely touched in over a year.

So before Friday, please email me your individual suggestions for improving it.
